crisis.label: Severe
crisis.detail: Jul 31: Direct US-Iran exchanges widen - US forces struck dozens of IRGC command, missile, drone, coastal-surveillance and defence targets in a two-hour heavy wave after Iran attacked a US base in Jordan. Iran then launched another barrage: Jordan intercepted five missiles for a second consecutive day, while a strike on a Chinese company's building in Kuwait killed one worker; Iranian media reported three killed and two wounded by US strikes on Qeshm Island (AP, Jul 30). Hormuz traffic fell from 82 ships in Jul 13-19 to 39 in Jul 20-26, according to Lloyd's List Intelligence cited by AP. Brent $88.00 (-0.41%, Yahoo Finance BZ=F, Jul 31); tail raised to 70%.

todaysEvents.summary: US strikes dozens of IRGC targets
todaysEvents.delta: Up: US forces completed a two-hour heavy wave against IRGC command, missile, drone, coastal-surveillance and defence targets after Iran attacked a US base in Jordan. Iranian media reported three killed and two wounded on Qeshm. Source: AP, Jul 30.

Up: Jordan intercepted five Iranian missiles for a second consecutive day. An Iranian strike hit a Chinese company's building in Kuwait, killing one worker. Both countries host US forces. Source: AP, Jul 30.
Up: Lloyd's List Intelligence counted 39 ships through Hormuz in Jul 20-26, down from 82 in Jul 13-19. Energy shipments remain near a halt. Source: AP citing Lloyd's List Intelligence, Jul 30.

scenarios.label: Base
scenarios.description: Mediators restore a temporary pause after the latest exchange and restart an Omani-led channel focused on Hormuz. A phased shipping arrangement gradually lowers the risk premium and Brent settles toward $80-90/bbl. Probability cut from 10% to 5% because the response has widened from proxy sites to direct US strikes on Iran and Iranian attacks across Jordan and Kuwait.

scenarios.label: Stress
scenarios.description: The direct exchange continues but remains bounded to military targets and regional bases, avoiding sustained attacks on Gulf energy infrastructure. Hormuz remains constrained at wartime-low traffic, keeping Brent in a volatile $90-110/bbl range and TTF elevated. Probability cut from 30% to 25% as attacks have widened geographically and direct US strikes on Iran have resumed.

scenarios.label: Tail
scenarios.description: Repeated US waves expand against IRGC and strategic targets while Iran broadens missile and drone attacks across US-allied Gulf states and commercial shipping. Saudi involvement and attacks on Jordan and Kuwait raise the risk of direct strikes on energy infrastructure and further closure of Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb. Brent spikes $100-140+/bbl and JKM exceeds $30/MMBtu. Probability raised from 60% to 70% after direct exchanges resumed at scale.
